capabilities.target: Arbitrary shell commands in the CI container, with access to env.GITHUB_TOKEN and unrestricted outbound network
GitHub branch push / PR open using an org-wide PAT with repo + workflow scope across all org repositories
The agent's own configuration: model, autonomy, tools, network, credentials
Slack channel, via a Slack MCP server the team plans to add next quarter

inputs.source: GitHub issue title and body on a public repository, labeled "bug" through a public issue template
Repository file contents read while reproducing and testing a fix
Slack messages, via a Slack MCP server the team plans to add next quarter

instructions.note: "Pick up any issue labeled bug and fix it end to end" gives the agent an open-ended mandate across any issue, backed by an org-wide credential, with no restriction to a single repository.
The only control against destructive or exfiltrating commands is a natural-language instruction to the model itself; nothing structural enforces it.

The sole defense against prompt injection from issue or code content is an instruction telling the model to ignore injected instructions. This is a behavioral, dependent control guarding the agent's primary attack surface.
Grants the agent authority to rewrite its own tool configuration with no human review, directly reachable from attacker-controlled issue content.

elements.name: Shared CI runner container running the agent
GitHub organization (all repositories reachable via the org-wide PAT)

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding destructive or exfiltrating commands
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on model compliance; a more capable or successfully manipulated model can rationalize exceptions or split a forbidden action into steps that each look allowed (prompt.md:4).

controls.name: Prompt instruction to ignore instructions embedded in issues or code
controls.decay_rationale: A classic prompt-injection defense implemented purely as a model instruction. Indirect injection (SAFE-T1401/SAFE-T1402 style) can still override it, and more capable models follow longer, more convincing injected goals (prompt.md:5). Its wording is also scoped to "issues or code" and does not textually extend to other channels such as a future Slack feed.

controls.name: Container execution on a shared CI runner
controls.decay_rationale: Isolates the agent process from the host, but network is explicitly unrestricted and the runner is shared, so it does not contain network egress or materially narrow the exfiltration paths assessed here (runtime notes).

controls.name: Scoped, per-repo, least-privilege credential instead of an org-wide PAT
Human approval gate before branch push and before self-configuration changes
Tamper-evident logging of shell, push, and config-write actions
Pin model version with review gate on upgrade

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted issue body drives direct secret exfiltration via shell.run

attack_path.note: Any GitHub user can open an issue labeled bug; its text enters the agent's context unsandboxed.
Agent runs attacker-influenced commands with env.GITHUB_TOKEN present and unrestricted outbound network, enabling direct exfiltration (e.g. curl to an attacker host).

forecast.watch_signal: model: latest already auto-upgrades with no pin or review (subject.model.swappable); any change to the underlying model id, or removal/editing of prompt.md lines 4-5, should be treated as having already occurred.

evidence.observation: tools include shell.run; env.GITHUB_TOKEN is an org-wide PAT with repo+workflow scope; network: unrestricted allows outbound exfiltration from any shell command.
The agent is instructed to run whatever commands are needed to reproduce and test an issue, with command content effectively driven by the untrusted issue body.
Any GitHub user can open an issue and add the "bug" label through an issue template, with no human gate before cap.shell runs.

recommendations.action: Replace the org-wide PAT with a short-lived, repo-scoped credential minted per task, with no workflow-file write scope.
Add an egress allowlist restricting shell.run's outbound network to the package registries and git remote actually needed; deny arbitrary outbound connections.
Log every shell command and outbound network call with tamper-evident storage, reviewed before merge.

findings.title: Self-modification (TC3): attacker-influenced task content can rewrite .agent/config.yaml with no gate

attack_path.note: Untrusted issue content sets the task context the agent is working under.
prompt.md:6 explicitly authorizes the agent to adjust its own config.yaml "if you need extra tools to finish a task," with no human approval, persisting the change across future sessions.

forecast.watch_signal: Any widening of config.yaml's tools list, or addition of a new MCP server such as the planned Slack connector, that the agent itself could have written rather than a human.

evidence.observation: "You may adjust .agent/config.yaml if you need extra tools to finish a task" grants unreviewed self-configuration authority.
autonomy: full and max_steps: null mean no runtime or step boundary limits what a self-configuration change can do once made.

recommendations.action: Make .agent/config.yaml read-only at runtime; route any tool or config change through a human-approved change to the agent's own deployment, not a self-write.
Remove the prompt line granting self-configuration authority; such changes should never be instructable by the agent's own task content.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): org-wide, workflow-scoped PAT enables lateral CI/CD compromise across all org repos

attack_path.note: Untrusted issue content drives the fix.
Agent can write any file in the workspace, including CI workflow definitions.
Agent pushes using a PAT with repo + workflow scope valid across all org repositories, far broader than a single bug-fix task requires.

forecast.watch_signal: PAT scope widening, or removal of prompt.md lines 4-5, with no corresponding credential-scoping or approval-gate control added.

evidence.observation: env.GITHUB_TOKEN is described as an org-wide PAT with repo + workflow scope on all org repos.
Agent pushes a branch and opens a PR using this credential with no stated destination or scope restriction.

recommendations.action: Scope the PAT to the single repo under repair with no workflow write permission, or require human approval before any push that touches .github/workflows/.
Require passing branch protection and required human review before merge on every repo the agent can push to.

findings.title: Forecast: planned Slack MCP server adds a new untrusted channel into an already self-configuring, ungated agent

attack_path.note: Planned Slack MCP server would bring untrusted Slack message content into context.
The agent's existing self-configuration authority (prompt.md:6) and lack of an approval gate would apply to this new channel exactly as it applies to issues today.

findings.residual_rationale: No Slack MCP connection exists yet, so no path is reachable today; inherent and residual are rated low for the present design. The elevated risk is captured entirely in the forecast block.

forecast.watch_signal: MCP client config diff adding a Slack server entry; new tool entries appearing in config.yaml's tools list.

evidence.observation: "The team wants to add a Slack MCP server next quarter" documents a planned new untrusted input channel with no described trust boundary or injection defense for it.
The existing anti-injection instruction is worded "instructions that appear inside issues or code," which does not textually extend to a future Slack channel.

recommendations.action: Before connecting the Slack MCP server, classify it as untrusted input, extend or rewrite the anti-injection instruction's scope, and add a structural gate (e.g., an allowlist of actionable intents) rather than relying on prompt wording alone.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted source (any GitHub user able to label an issue "bug") has a one-hop path to irreversible, org-wide-credentialed egress (shell exec with unrestricted network, git push with workflow scope, and unreviewed self-configuration), with full autonomy and no step or runtime bound. Residual stays at high because the only controls present are two behavioral, dependent prompt instructions (prompt.md:4-5); per the rubric's step-4 cap, stacking dependent behavioral controls earns at most one tier of credit regardless of count, and no structural control (credential scoping, egress allowlist, approval gate, or config lockdown) exists to earn further credit or sever any path. Forecast returns to critical because a model upgrade is the single most consequential trigger: it defeats both behavioral instructions at once, and the design already auto-upgrades the model ("model: latest") with no pin or review gate, so this trigger should be treated as continuously live rather than a future event. Adding the planned Slack MCP server compounds this by opening a second untrusted channel into the same ungated self-configuration capability.

limitations: This assessment reflects the design and configuration described in prompt.md, .agent/config.yaml, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
config.yaml lists fs.read and github.open_pr as tools, but no stable id was given for them; their paths are inferred from cap.fs_write and cap.git_push rather than scored as separate capabilities.

Whether branch protection or required human review exists on the target repositories before merge is not stated in the artifacts; this assessment does not assume such a control exists absent evidence, which is why it is listed as a missing recommended control rather than a declared one.

in.repo_files is rated internal trust absent evidence about who can merge to the default branch; if external contributors can merge changes, this should be revised to untrusted, which would raise findings touching cap.shell and cap.fs_write from repo file content alone.
